minutes.headline: Assessors keep the FY27 overlay at its proposed level and set a September deadline for the new senior tax exemption
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors welcomed the town's new financial director/accountant and walked through how the senior means-tested tax exemption, overlay, and MUNIS issues have been handled. Most of the meeting was routine business: signing excise and abatement paperwork, correcting and approving a backlog of minutes, fixing errors in the draft annual report, and reviewing ongoing problems with parcel mapping, chapter land, and sewer betterments. The board decided to keep its proposed FY2027 overlay unchanged, set a fixed annual deadline for the senior means-tested exemption, and adopted a board code of conduct policy.

what_happened.line: The board voted to leave the proposed FY2027 overlay unchanged despite fewer abatement requests, citing expected cost increases from expanded exemptions and pending neighborhood-factor corrections.
The board voted to set the senior means-tested tax exemption application deadline as the first Wednesday in September, going forward.
The board voted to adopt a code of conduct policy for its members.
A planned upgrade to the town's mapping/GIS software was dropped for FY2027 for budget reasons.
The new town accountant will research a property-tax "shift" mechanism for the senior exemption before next year's classification hearing.

why_it_matters: The overlay is the reserve set aside to cover abatements against the tax levy, so holding it steady rather than shrinking it affects how the tax rate is set even though fewer abatements were requested this year.
Homeowners who qualify for the senior means-tested exemption now have one fixed annual deadline, the first Wednesday in September, to file their application.
Dropping the mapping/GIS software upgrade may leave known parcel-mapping accuracy issues unaddressed for another year, which can affect individual assessments.
watch_next: The March 12 Senior Center presentation on the senior tax exemption programs
The accountant's research on the property-tax "shift" mechanism, expected before the next classification hearing

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the meeting's two substantive votes (the exemption due-date and the code-of-conduct adoption) and on several headline figures (the $260,000 overlay budget, the $1,819,740.97 excise commitment), but they cover different slices of the meeting: ours captures far more of the discussion-stage dollar figures while the official minutes alone record the executive session, the formal roll-call votes on minutes/abatements, and several status-report statistics. The most consequential thing to check is the board chair — our minutes attribute the chair title to "Brian Marle," but the official minutes list Brian Laffond as Chair and Brian Marple as a plain Member.
